chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) did not take the inheritance of any of his mawali if he died and had relatives; he would give it to his relatives."
ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali take the inheritance of his mawali if they had relatives?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) adherence to the principle of *qarabah* (kinship) over the *mawaliyyah* (clientage) bond, demonstrating his preference for distributing wealth to blood relatives rather than claiming it as a former master. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that while the master retains a share, the presence of close kin takes precedence in practical application, reflecting the Prophet’s tradition of prioritizing familial ties. It serves as a key evidence in discussions regarding the distribution of inheritance between the *mu'all* (freedman) and his *mawla* (patron).
